newHazards.summary: Narrowing the off-list refusal opens a UI route to subscribe() with an unrankable key, which writes the plan enum shadow as STARTER and leaves the row ranking as STARTER
newHazards.detail: Newly reachable consequence of hazard 6's fix, one step past the pin. With an off-list definition published (planKey "PRO"), a TRIAL/non-ACTIVE tenant now gets action SUBSCRIBE instead of a 400, so the chooser renders a working commit control that posts /billing/subscribe. subscribe() accepts it — the catalog check at :173 passes because the definition exists — and writes planKey:"PRO" with basePriceSnapshot 199 (correct, as the design assumed) but ALSO currentPlan: planKeyToEnum("PRO"), which falls through normalizePlanKey→null to the `default: return "STARTER"` at plan-catalog.constants.ts:199-209, and the same value onto Tenant.plan. From then on resolveFromPlanKey("PRO", "STARTER") returns "STARTER" (normalizePlanKey null, then planKeyFromEnum), so the tenant ranks as STARTER while paying 199: a later upgrade() nets amountDelta against planMonthly(version, "STARTER") rather than 199, booking an inflated MRR delta, and planChangePreview will classify moves off it against STARTER's rank. Scored minor because it requires an operational publishing error (a definition whose key is outside PLAN_KEYS), and the POST /billing/subscribe endpoint was already directly callable with such a key before this round — what round 4 adds is the UI door. If the owner wants it closed without reinstating the blanket 400, the narrow move is a `planRank(input.planKey) < 0` refusal inside subscribe(), mirroring downgrade():690-692.

newHazards.summary: A failed re-quote now makes the summary card vanish with no message — useQuote has no error toast and the page passes only clearPreview
newHazards.detail: Introduced by hazard 4's fix. useQuote (lib/api/billing.ts:198-202) is a bare useMutation with no onError, and the page's only handler for a failed quote is `clearPreview` (:78, :86), which sets preview to null. Because the summary card is gated on `preview &&` at :264, a tenant who has a quote on screen and then toggles MONTHLY↔ANNUAL into a failing request sees the entire Summary block — figures, warning line, commit button — disappear with no toast and no error text, while the plan card still reads "Selected". The money behaviour is right (fail-closed: nothing stale is committable, which is the point of the ruling) and the first-pick failure was already silent before this round, so this is a UX residual, not a correctness defect. Closing it is one line: pass an onError that both clears and toasts (the page already has `toast` in scope and uses the same server-message extraction at :137-145 for commit failures).

newHazards.summary: The Playwright quote fixture builds `change` without the new required seatAckRequired, so the only end-to-end consumer never exercises the ack path
newHazards.detail: L-072-class test-fidelity drift left by this round. quoteBody() at :103-129 fulfils /billing/quote with a hand-written `change` object — `{action:"DOWNGRADE", effectiveAt, proratedNow:null}` — that omits seatAckRequired, which the web mirror now declares REQUIRED. It is raw JSON inside route.fulfill, so neither tsc nor the web Jest suite catches the omission. Consequence: the DOWNGRADE routing test at :239-268 passes precisely because seatAckRequired is absent (=== true is false, so no checkbox blocks the click), and it would keep passing unchanged if the API regressed the field to optional or dropped it entirely — the exact regression the seam was built to prevent. The e2e also cannot cover the over-cap case at all. Not a product defect and not a gate failure (the design's pins for hazard 1 are API-side), but the fixture should gain `seatAckRequired: false` on both branches, and ideally a third case with `seatAckRequired: true` asserting the commit stays disabled until the checkbox is ticked.

review.reasoning: All five in-scope hazards survive refutation as genuinely fixed, and the deferred one was left untouched exactly as the design required. The seam that the round existed to build is consistent in both directions and I checked it both ways rather than taking the executors' word: seatAckRequired is required on the API interface and present on all seven return sites of planChangePreview (no eighth return exists), it passes through settings-billing.controller.ts's quote handler unfiltered, it is required on the web mirror, and the page reads it with a strict === true so mirror drift fails closed to no acknowledgement rather than to a false one. I traced the flag against billing-cron's applyScheduledDowngrades line by line — same pinned catalog version, same seat cap, same user.count where-clause, same > comparison — so it fires exactly when the sweep deactivates staff, which is the property the whole ruling rests on. The L-072 sweep found no remaining web-only field: message is gone from both the interface and the render, and the only asymmetry left (fromPlanKey optional on web, required on the API) is pre-existing and in the safe direction. The three specific new-hazard shapes the brief asked me to hunt all came back clean: no stale-preview path escapes the two onError handlers (setPreview has exactly two callers and the only non-null one resets ackDowngrade), the warning-composition change is byte-identical in the nothing-armed case and pinned with toBe, and the moved unknown-key guard leaves no ranking path unguarded since every consumer of toKey is downstream of line 445. The three new hazards I did find are all minor and none blocks landing: one needs an operational publishing error to reach and was already reachable at the API before this round, one is a UX silence rather than a money defect, and one is test-fixture fidelity in a post-deploy Playwright project. Round 4 fixed four real defects, the gates are green on both apps, and another round would buy three minor residuals that are better carried as close-out rows than paid for with a fifth cycle on a working tree that has been open three rounds. Land, and record the off-list subscribe() ranking residual and the e2e fixture gap where the deferred hazard 5 row goes.
